harness_rules: Fixtures with "withdrawn": true MUST be skipped, never executed (v3 §8.4).
Fixtures with "deferred": true MUST be skipped until "blocked_on" is satisfied, and their skip MUST be reported rather than counted as a pass (v3 §8 row 17b).
The entry with "kind": "assertion" is a meta-assertion over the other fixtures, not a data fixture; dispatch on it rather than parsing an external value.

Fixtures are keyed by (id, part). "part" is absent for every fixture except the two halves of 17, which are (17, "a") and (17, "b"). This keeps "id" an integer for typed loaders rather than mixing int and string, while keeping ids traceable to v3 §8's numbering (v3 §8.2).

Human-facing output (test names, reports) MUST use the derived display key: str(id) + (part or "") -> "5", "17a", "17b". Uniqueness is asserted on (id, part); the display form is presentation only and is never a key (v3 §8.2).
Reports MUST state both counts from "counts" below — 25 executable data fixtures AND 26 harness assertions today — so "25" is never read as "the harness runs 25 things" (v3 §8.1).

Fixtures 23-28 exercise the v3 §3b treatment suffix. The suffix is LOWERCASE in both the internal and external forms (v3 §4 rule 6), and the set component of an OP product code is the mirrored BASE SET (ogs-019-024-champion), never 'op' — see v3 §3b and §8.4. Resolving an OP code to its base set is a tcgplayer_groups data lookup, not a grammar rule (fixture 28, deferred).

"harness_assertions_today" counts what the harness actually runs today. Always report "executable_today" (25) and "harness_assertions_today" (26) together. These figures were 20 and 21 until 2026-08-16, when v3 §3b added fixtures 23-28; anything quoting the older pair predates the treatment suffix.

casing_rule: v3 §4, internal -> external: (1) uppercase the SET component; (2) uppercase the NUMBER's alphabetic prefix if present (r->R, t->T, sp->SP); (3) preserve the variant suffix letter in lowercase; (4) preserve the asterisk verbatim; (5) insert '/' before TOTAL when present. External -> internal is unchanged: lowercase everything.
set_codes_are_data: v3 §3: the parser MUST NOT validate the set component against any enumeration. Any 2-4 letter set is accepted; whether it exists is answered by the join, not the regex. A well-formed code for an unknown set is situation C (data gap), not situation A (malformed).

FORWARD-LOOKING, zero occurrences in either population as of 2026-08-16; do not delete as redundant (same standing as fixture 18). Asserts the one grammar path fixtures 23-25 cannot reach: treatment present while TOTAL is ABSENT. Runes carry no total (v3 §3), so this is where an implementation that splits on '-', or that assumes the segment after the number is always the total, breaks. No product with this code is known to exist; it exercises the grammar, not the catalogue.

v3 §3b. An all-digit treatment component MUST fail to parse. TOTAL is also digits, so a numeric component makes 'ven-r01-8' irresolvably ambiguous between 'total 8' and 'treatment 8'. The correct slug for the observed treatment 'Top 8' is 'top8', because slug step 2 deletes the space — so this state is unreachable through the slug rule and is rejected by the grammar as well. Unrepresentable beats merely prohibited.

DEFERRED. Resolving an OP product code to its mirrored base set is a DATA lookup through tcgplayer_groups, not a grammar rule, and must not be implemented as one. It is tempting to read the base set off TOTAL (024 -> OGS); v3 §12 warns explicitly that this works only because the five set totals happen to be distinct today — a coincidence, not a property, which breaks the first time two sets share a total. The seven known OP holdings are tabulated in v3 §8.4 and were re-verified against live 2026-08-16 (OP-011/024 = Flash = ogs-011-024). Harness must skip and REPORT the skip, never count it as a pass. This entry, not fixture 13, is the live successor to what 13 was reaching for.
